objetivo: That the student recognizes that a force is a push or a pull, that forces can move, stop, or change the direction of objects, and that gravity and friction are forces that act every day.
hatsumon: Why does a ball rolling on the floor eventually stop on its own?

turnos.utterance_formal: Today we're going to study why things move and why they stop.
turnos.utterance_coloquial: Today we're going to study why things move and why they stop.

turnos.utterance_formal: Get out your notebook; today we're going to make several drawings with arrows.
turnos.utterance_coloquial: Get out your notebook; today we're gonna make a bunch of drawings with arrows.

turnos.utterance_formal: Think about this: why does a ball rolling on the floor eventually stop on its own?
turnos.utterance_coloquial: Okay, think about it: why does a ball rolling on the floor just stop by itself?

turnos.utterance_formal: Hold on to your answer; we'll answer it properly at the end.
turnos.utterance_coloquial: Hold on to your answer; we'll answer it properly at the end.

turnos.utterance_formal: Nothing moves by itself: something has to push it or pull it.
turnos.utterance_coloquial: Nothing moves by itself: something has to push it or pull it.

operations.text: Nothing moves by itself: something has to push it or pull it

turnos.utterance_formal: We call that push or pull that moves things a force.
turnos.utterance_coloquial: So that push or pull that moves things? We call it force.

set.text: Nothing moves by itself: something has to push it or pull it, and that push or pull is called a **force**.

turnos.utterance_formal: We don't always see the force, but we do see what it does.
turnos.utterance_coloquial: We don't always see the force, but we do see what it does.

set.text: Nothing moves by itself: something has to push it or pull it, and that push or pull is called a **force**. We don't always see a force, only what it does.

turnos.utterance_formal: The first way to apply force is pushing: we move the object away from us.
turnos.utterance_coloquial: The first way to apply force is pushing: we move the object away from us.

set.text: Nothing moves by itself: something has to push it or pull it, and that push or pull is called a **force**. We don't always see a force, only what it does. **Pushing** moves an object away from us.

turnos.utterance_formal: Watch: a boy pushes a box to move it forward.
turnos.utterance_coloquial: Check it out: a kid pushes a box to move it forward.

turnos.utterance_formal: The box moves away from him, in the direction of the push.
turnos.utterance_coloquial: The box moves away from him, in whatever direction he pushed it.

turnos.utterance_formal: The other way is pulling: we bring the object toward us.
turnos.utterance_coloquial: The other way is pulling: we bring the object toward us.

turnos.utterance_formal: Now the same boy pulls a little cart toward him.
turnos.utterance_coloquial: Now the same boy pulls a little cart toward him.

turnos.utterance_formal: Push and pull: they're both forces, they just go in opposite directions.
turnos.utterance_coloquial: Push and pull: they're both forces, they just go opposite ways from each other.

operations.text: Push and pull are both forces, but they act in opposite directions.

turnos.utterance_formal: So now we have the two ways to apply force: push and pull.
turnos.utterance_coloquial: So now we have the two ways to apply force: push and pull.

turnos.utterance_formal: Now, what does a force do to an object? It can do three things.
turnos.utterance_coloquial: Now, what does a force do to an object? It can do three things.

operations.text: A **force** can do three things to an object

turnos.utterance_formal: A force does three things: it moves what's still, stops what's moving, changes the direction.
turnos.utterance_coloquial: A force does three things: it moves what's still, stops what's moving, changes the direction.

operations.text:
Moves what's still
Stops what's moving
Changes the direction

turnos.utterance_formal: If you kick a ball that's sitting still, the force sets it moving.
turnos.utterance_coloquial: If you hit a ball that's sitting still, the force sets it moving.

turnos.utterance_formal: Haven't you seen a ball start rolling the second you touch it?
turnos.utterance_coloquial: Haven't you seen a ball start rolling the second you touch it?

turnos.utterance_formal: And if it hits a wall, the wall pushes back with a force and stops it.
turnos.utterance_coloquial: And if it hits a wall, the wall pushes back with a force and stops it.

turnos.utterance_formal: And a force can also change the shape of something soft, like clay.
turnos.utterance_coloquial: And a force can also change the shape of something soft, like clay.

operations.text: A force can also change the **shape** of something soft, like clay.

turnos.utterance_formal: Pay attention to the three things a force can do, that's the important part.
turnos.utterance_coloquial: Pay attention to the three things a force can do, that's the important part.

turnos.utterance_formal: There's a force that's acting all the time without us seeing it: gravity.
turnos.utterance_coloquial: There's a force that's acting all the time without us seeing it: gravity.

turnos.utterance_formal: If you let go of an apple, gravity pulls it and it falls to the ground.
turnos.utterance_coloquial: If you let go of an apple, gravity pulls it down and it falls to the ground.

turnos.utterance_formal: Because of gravity, things don't just stay floating in the air.
turnos.utterance_coloquial: Because of gravity, things don't just stay floating in the air.

operations.text: Because of gravity, things don't just stay floating in the air

turnos.utterance_formal: Has your pencil ever fallen? Well, that was gravity.
turnos.utterance_coloquial: Ever had your pencil just drop on you? Yeah, that was gravity.

set.text: Because of gravity, things don't just stay floating in the air, like a pencil that falls off the desk.

turnos.utterance_formal: So far we've got push, pull, gravity... take a look at those forces.
turnos.utterance_coloquial: So far we've got push, pull, gravity... check out those forces.

turnos.utterance_formal: There's one left that answers our question: friction, which slows down movement.
turnos.utterance_coloquial: There's one left that answers our question: friction, which slows down movement.

turnos.utterance_formal: It shows up when two surfaces rub against each other, like the ball against the floor.
turnos.utterance_coloquial: It shows up when two sur faces rub against each other, like the ball against the floor.

set.text: A force that **slows down** movement, and it shows up when two surfaces rub against each other.

turnos.utterance_formal: Watch a marble going down a ramp: friction slows it down little by little.
turnos.utterance_coloquial: Watch a marble going down a ramp: fric tion slows it down little by little.

turnos.utterance_formal: The rougher the surface, the more friction it makes.
turnos.utterance_coloquial: The rougher the sur face, the more friction it makes.

operations.text: The rougher the surface, the more **friction** it makes

turnos.utterance_formal: And that's how we answer it: the ball that rolls stops because of friction with the floor.
turnos.utterance_coloquial: And that's how we answer it: the ball that rolls stops because of friction with the floor.

set.text: The rougher the surface, the more **friction** it makes, so the ball that rolls stops because of friction with the floor

turnos.utterance_formal: Go back and look at the question from the beginning: it's already answered.
turnos.utterance_coloquial: Go back and look at the question from the beginning: it's already answered.

turnos.utterance_formal: Without friction, everything would slide forever, like on ice.
turnos.utterance_coloquial: Without friction, everything would slide forever, like on ice.

set.text: The rougher the surface, the more **friction** it makes, so the ball that rolls stops because of friction with the floor, and without friction everything would slide forever.

turnos.utterance_formal: That's why we slip on ice: there's almost no friction.
turnos.utterance_coloquial: That's why we slip on ice: there's almost no friction.

turnos.utterance_formal: Hold on to today's big idea, the one that sums everything up.
turnos.utterance_coloquial: Hold on to that big idea for today, the one that wraps it all up.

operations.text: A **force** is a push or a pull

turnos.utterance_formal: And with what it does: it moves, stops, or changes the direction of objects.
turnos.utterance_coloquial: And with what it does: it moves, stops, or changes the direction of objects.

set.text: A **force** is a push or a pull, which can move, stop, or redirect objects.

turnos.utterance_formal: And today's big word, the one you shouldn't forget, is force.
turnos.utterance_coloquial: And today's big word, the one you shouldn't forget, is force.

set.text: A **force** is a push or a pull, which can move, stop, or redirect objects. The key word is **force**.

turnos.utterance_formal: Remember what a force is: a push or a pull.
turnos.utterance_coloquial: Remember what a force is: a push or a pull.

turnos.utterance_formal: Rest your hand for a moment and then we'll wrap up.
turnos.utterance_coloquial: Give your hand a little break and then we'll wrap up.

turnos.utterance_formal: Take one last look at the four forces we drew today.
turnos.utterance_coloquial: Take one last look at the four forces we drew today.

turnos.utterance_formal: Does everyone have their arrows drawn? Perfect.
turnos.utterance_coloquial: Does everyone have their little arrows drawn? Alright, perfect.

turnos.utterance_formal: For homework, write down three things that push and three that pull in your day.
turnos.utterance_coloquial: Okay so for homework, write down three things that push and three that pull in your day.

operations.text: Write 3 things you push and 3 things you pull.

turnos.utterance_formal: And explain to me why a bike gradually slows down when you stop pedaling.
turnos.utterance_coloquial: And explain to me why a bike gradually slows down when you stop pedaling.

turnos.utterance_coloquial: Alright, I can see that's super clear. Excellent work.

turnos.utterance_coloquial: That's it for today. Put your stuff away and I'll see you all tomorrow.
